effects: Takes exactly `assets` USDC from the signer and sends it to the vault (enter: safeTransferFrom(asset, msg.sender, address(this), assets)).
Mints armUSDCp shares to `onBehalf`. The amount is previewDeposit(assets), set by the share price at execution. There is no minimum-shares parameter.
Accrues interest first, which can mint fee shares to the fee recipients. This dilutes the share price used for the signer's deposit.
formats.shown: Deposit 100000 USDC for <onBehalf>, with fields for the USDC amount, the share ticker armUSDCp and the share recipient.

findings.title: deposit: the number of armUSDCp shares received is not shown; it is computed on-chain with no minimum.
findings.evidence: VaultV2.sol deposit(): `uint256 shares = previewDeposit(assets);`. Case 0: the signer received 100000 armUSDCp, and the screen shows only 'Share ticker: armUSDCp'.
findings.fix: None possible in the descriptor: the share amount is not in calldata and the function has no minShares argument.

findings.title: deposit: the interpolated intent says 'for <address>' but not that armUSDCp shares go to that address.
findings.evidence: descriptor interpolatedIntent "Deposit {#.assets} for {#.onBehalf}"; the code mints shares to onBehalf: `createShares(onBehalf, shares)`.
findings.fix: Use "Deposit {#.assets} and send armUSDCp shares to {#.onBehalf}".

cases.notes: The 100000 USDC out is shown exactly. The 100000 armUSDCp in is shown with its asset and recipient but no amount, which cannot be known from calldata.

formats.key: withdraw(uint256 assets, address receiver, address onBehalf)
effects: Burns armUSDCp shares from `onBehalf`. The amount is previewWithdraw(assets), rounded up, and there is no maximum-shares parameter.
Sends exactly `assets` USDC from the vault to `receiver`.
If the signer is not `onBehalf`, spends the signer's armUSDCp allowance from `onBehalf` by the shares burned.
Accrues interest first (fee shares can be minted) and may pull liquidity back from the liquidity adapter. Neither changes the amount sent to the receiver.
formats.shown: Withdraw 50 USDC to <receiver>, with fields for the exact USDC amount, the recipient and the owner whose position is used.

findings.title: withdraw: the number of armUSDCp shares burned is not shown; it is computed on-chain with no cap.
findings.evidence: VaultV2.sol withdraw(): `uint256 shares = previewWithdraw(assets);` then exit() calls deleteShares(onBehalf, shares). Case 2: 49.658176641164756842 armUSDCp left the signer, and no field states a share amount.
findings.fix: None possible in the descriptor: the share amount is not in calldata and there is no maxShares argument.

findings.title: withdraw: the interpolated intent omits the owner whose armUSDCp shares are burned.
findings.evidence: descriptor interpolatedIntent "Withdraw {#.assets} to {#.receiver}"; exit(): `deleteShares(onBehalf, shares)` and the allowance is spent when msg.sender != onBehalf. Owner appears only as a field.

cases.notes: The 50 USDC in to the signer is shown exactly. The armUSDCp burn (49.66 shares) is not shown; the reader only inferred that the position shrinks by about 50 USDC.

formats.key: redeem(uint256 shares, address receiver, address onBehalf)
effects: Burns exactly `shares` armUSDCp from `onBehalf`. If the signer is not `onBehalf`, the signer's share allowance from `onBehalf` is spent.
Sends USDC from the vault to `receiver`. The amount is previewRedeem(shares), rounded down, and there is no minimum-assets parameter.
Accrues interest first (fee shares can be minted) and may pull liquidity back from the liquidity adapter.
formats.shown: Redeem <shares> armUSDCp to <receiver>, with fields for the share amount, the recipient and the owner. Nothing names USDC as the asset received.

findings.title: redeem: the USDC amount received is not shown; it is computed on-chain with no minimum.
findings.evidence: VaultV2.sol redeem(): `uint256 assets = previewRedeem(shares);`. Case 3: the signer received 20652.648916 USDC, and no field states it.
findings.fix: None possible for the amount: it is not in calldata and the function has no minAssets argument.

findings.title: redeem: the screen never says the signer receives USDC; the asset is known but not displayed.
findings.evidence: exit(): `SafeERC20Lib.safeTransfer(asset, receiver, assets)` with asset = USDC (constant underlyingTicker). The redeem fields show only shares, To and Owner. Case 3 reader: 'The screen doesn't show the amount or token. The name suggests USDC.'
findings.fix: Add a constant field 'Receive asset' = $.metadata.constants.underlyingTicker (as mint already does) and use the intent "Redeem {#.shares} for USDC to {#.receiver}".

findings.title: redeem: the interpolated intent omits the owner whose shares are burned.
findings.evidence: descriptor interpolatedIntent "Redeem {#.shares} to {#.receiver}"; exit() burns from onBehalf and spends the allowance when msg.sender != onBehalf.

cases.notes: The 20560.586 armUSDCp out is shown exactly. The 20652.65 USDC in has no amount and no asset on screen; the reader guessed USDC from the name.

findings.title: mint: the intent 'Mint' does not say USDC leaves the signer's wallet to pay for the shares.

findings.fix: Use intent "Deposit USDC for shares" and interpolatedIntent "Deposit USDC to mint {#.shares} for {#.onBehalf}".
